sections.title: State licensing and registration
sections.markdown: **No chimney or sweep license exists in Mississippi.** STATE LAW: the MS State Board of Contractors (MSBOC) licenses **Residential Builders (new residential construction when "the total cost of the undertaking exceeds Fifty Thousand Dollars ($50,000.00)")** and **Remodelers (improvements to an existing residence when "the total cost of the improvements exceeds Ten Thousand Dollars ($10,000.00)")** under **Miss. Code Ann. § 73-59-1 et seq.** (definitions, § 73-59-1, 2025 Code: https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-73/chapter-59/section-73-59-1/). The Board's FAQ states the same lines — a residential license is needed for "new residential construction over $50,000, residential remodeling or additions over $10,000, or residential roofing over $10,000" (https://www.msboc.us/general-info/frequently-asked-questions/). Commercial side is Title 31 ch. 3. **Most chimney work (sweeps $150–400, caps, crown/flashing repairs, many relines) sits at or under the $10,000 remodeler line — no state credential required at all.** Public lookup: **Contractor Search at https://www.msboc.us** (800-880-6161), confirmed as the AG's own recommended check (REF: https://magnoliatribune.com/2022/05/31/ag-fitch-and-ms-board-of-contractors-urge-mississippians-to-beware-of-contractor-schemes-as-hurricane-season-begins/). Unlicensed work over threshold: **misdemeanor, fine of $100–$5,000 or 30–60 days imprisonment** (§ 73-59-9, https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-73/chapter-59/section-73-59-9/). What the license rests on, per MSBOC's FAQ: all applicants take the **Mississippi Law and Business Management exam** (open book, PSI), plus a trade exam depending on classification; **general liability insurance is mandatory but "no minimum coverage requirement for residential license holders"**; the FAQ does not address a bond (do not publish a bond claim either way).

sections.title: What the credential does not test
sections.markdown: The residential license rests on a business/law exam plus classification trade exams — **none of it chimney-specific: no flue sizing, no NFPA 211 Level I/II inspection method, no clearance-to-combustibles**. Insurance is required but with no minimum amount for residential licensees. And since jobs of $10,000 or less need no credential whatsoever, the person on the roof may hold literally nothing. CSIA/NCSG individual certs are the only chimney-specific competence signal in the state (NATIONAL STANDARD framing; gap analysis medium confidence).

sections.title: Seller disclosure when a home sells
sections.markdown: STATE LAW: mandatory **Property Condition Disclosure Statement (PCDS)**, Miss. Code Ann. **§§ 89-1-501 through 89-1-527** (https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-89/chapter-1/real-estate-transfer-disclosure-requirements/section-89-1-509/), MREC-promulgated form that "may not be altered or personalized." Fetched the actual form (https://www.mrec.ms.gov/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/mrec_forms_PCDS_2017_FINAL-LEGAL_WITH_PAGE_NUMBERS-03-27-2017.pdf): **Section E.2 asks about "past or present problems, malfunctions or defects with … fireplace/chimneys … including any modifications to them"**; E.3 covers **outdoor fireplaces**; the Section G appliance grid lists **SMOKE/MONOXIDE DETECTORS and FREE STANDING STOVE**; B.7–B.8 ask whether remodels were permitted and name the licensed contractor. **Scope (confirmed in statute text):** § 89-1-501 applies to transfers of real property with 1–4 dwelling units (sale, exchange, installment land contract, lease with option, etc.) only "when the execution of such transfers is by, or with the aid of, a duly licensed real estate broker or salesperson" (https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-89/chapter-1/real-estate-transfer-disclosure-requirements/section-89-1-501/). **A true FSBO sale with no licensee involved is outside the statute** — the page must say so. **No inspection mandated at transfer.** Buyer inspection window is contract-custom, not statute — UNVERIFIED, typically negotiated in the purchase contract.

sections.title: Consumer remedies and cancellation rights
sections.markdown: STATE LAW: MS Consumer Protection Act, Miss. Code Ann. § 75-24-5 (UDAP). Private remedy (§ 75-24-15, https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-75/chapter-24/general-provisions/section-75-24-15/) is thin: **monetary loss only — NO treble damages, NO class actions ("every private action must be maintained in the name of and for the sole use and benefit of the individual person"), and plaintiff must FIRST make "a reasonable attempt to resolve any claim through an informal dispute settlement program approved by the Attorney General."** Complaints: AG Consumer Protection Division portal, https://attorneygenerallynnfitch.com/divisions/consumer-protection/ / consumer@ago.ms.gov. Two sharper teeth elsewhere: (1) **§ 73-59-9 — a builder/remodeler required to be licensed "who does not have the license ... at the time construction, building or remodeling services are rendered may not bring any action, either at law or in equity, to enforce any contract"**; recovery limited to "actual documented expenses for labor, materials or both," shown by clear and convincing evidence. *(Do not cite Lutz Homes v. Weston (Miss. 2009) for this rule: that case read the statute's earlier wording and let a builder licensed before suit counterclaim; the current text keys the bar to licensure when services are rendered.)* (2) **Criminal Home Repair Fraud, § 97-23-103** — the definition of "home repair" **explicitly lists "chimneys, chimney liners"**; first offense under $5,000 is a misdemeanor (up to $1,000 fine and/or 6 months), **felony up to 10 years when fraud is $10,000 or more**, mandatory restitution (https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-97/chapter-23/section-97-23-103/). 3-day cancel: **§ 75-66-3, home-solicitation sales, "until midnight of the third business day"** (https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-75/chapter-66/section-75-66-3/) — but cancellation is lost "if the buyer requests the seller to provide goods or services without delay because of an emergency, and (a) the seller in good faith makes a substantial beginning of performance of the contract before the buyer gives notice of cancellation, and (b) in the case of goods, the goods cannot be returned to the seller in substantially as good condition as when received by the buyer" — a loophole tailor-made for "emergency chimney repair" pitches.

sections.title: Permits and building codes
sections.confidenceNote: statute confirmed; current edition list STILL OPEN
sections.markdown: STATE LAW: SB 2378 (2014) created a **State Uniform Construction Code**, Miss. Code Ann. **§ 17-2-4** (Council: § 17-2-3; chapter: https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-17/chapter-2/). Jurisdictions subject to it must adopt **"one (1) of the last three (3) adopted editions" of the IBC or IRC** as amended by the MS Building Codes Council (§ 17-2-4, https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-17/chapter-2/section-17-2-4/). The **opt-out was a one-time window**: within 120 days of the section taking effect, a county board of supervisors or municipal governing authority could resolve not to be subject to it (the Insurance Department describes the deadline as Nov. 30, 2014: https://www.mid.ms.gov/sfmo/mississippi-uniform-building-codes/). A separate, older rule, **§ 17-2-1 (2006, post-Katrina)**, requires the coastal-area counties named there (Jackson, Harrison, Hancock, Stone, Pearl River) and their municipalities to adopt the latest IBC/IRC editions, again with a one-time opt-out. Because counties and cities could opt out, enforcement is a **patchwork** *(how many opted out is NOT verified — no primary source found; do not publish a share)*: LOCAL — Jackson, Gulfport, Biloxi, Hattiesburg and most cities permit and inspect; many rural counties have **no building department at all**. MID's **https://apps.mid.ms.gov/ubc/ubc.aspx** is a *reporting form* jurisdictions use to tell MID their code status under SB 2378 (2014) — not a public lookup; for a given jurisdiction's status, contact MID (601-359-1085) or the local building department. Where codes apply, reline/rebuild/wood-stove installs are mechanical/building permits under IRC ch. 10; **NFPA 211 is a NATIONAL STANDARD here, not adopted state law**. State Fire Prevention Code (§§ 45-11-101 – 45-11-111) governs state-owned/public buildings, not private homes.

sections.rawHeading: 6 · CO & smoke law (GOV — high confidence on the absence)
sections.title: Carbon monoxide and smoke alarm law
sections.markdown: **Mississippi has NO statewide smoke-alarm statute and NO CO-alarm statute for private dwellings.** The "Mississippi Smoke Detector Act" (SB 2782, 1999) **died in committee** (verified bill history: https://billstatus.ls.state.ms.us/1999/pdf/history/SB/SB2782.htm) — yet multiple consumer sites still quote its text as if enacted. Mississippi is **absent from NCSL's CO-detector statute table** (checked https://www.ncsl.org/environment-and-natural-resources/carbon-monoxide-detector-installation-statutes; page last updated Sep 29, 2025; REF). Requirements exist only where a jurisdiction adopted the IRC/IFC (new construction R314/R315: smoke alarms all bedrooms/levels; CO alarms with fuel-burning appliances or attached garages) — LOCAL, new-construction-focused. Rentals: § 89-8-23 landlord duty is only generic housing-code compliance. Enforcement reality: near zero outside permitted new builds. (2026-session check: the legislature's bill-status site still could not be fetched for 2026 on Sep 25, 2026 — see blockers.)

sections.title: Solid fuel and environmental rules
sections.markdown: **No state wood-stove emission or certification program** — EPA NSPS Step 2 (NATIONAL) governs new stove sales. No statewide spark-arrestor rule found. Burn restrictions are county-by-county: under **Miss. Code Ann. § 49-19-351**, when the Forestry Commission determines drought or wildfire conditions exist, the county board of supervisors may by order prohibit or restrict outdoor burning in the **unincorporated** parts of the county (knowing and willful violation: misdemeanor, **$100–$500**; enforced by the sheriff). The statute itself contains no grill exemption; the **Forestry Commission's burn-ban page** says propane/gas grills, propane/gas heaters and charcoal grills remain allowed during a ban — active bans at https://www.mfc.ms.gov/burning-info/burn-bans/ (statute: https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-49/chapter-19/restrictions-on-outdoor-burning/section-49-19-351/). Bans target outdoor fire, not indoor fireplaces.

sections.title: Scam patterns and enforcement
sections.markdown: No chimney-sweep-specific enforcement action found. The pattern is **storm-chaser home-repair fraud**: AG Fitch + Insurance Commissioner + MSBOC issue joint warnings each hurricane season and after tornado/winter events — verify license at msboc.us, written contract, never pay cash up front (2022 advisory: https://magnoliatribune.com/2022/05/31/ag-fitch-and-ms-board-of-contractors-urge-mississippians-to-beware-of-contractor-schemes-as-hurricane-season-begins/; AG storm-victim tips PDF: https://attorneygenerallynnfitch.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Tips-for-Storm-Victims.pdf). Prosecutors also have the § 97-23-103 criminal hammer (chimneys named in the statute). Name no companies — no public chimney enforcement action surfaced.

sections.title: Season calendar
sections.markdown: Humid subtropical; short burn season roughly **Nov–Feb** (north MS hills colder than the Gulf Coast). Rush: **Oct–Dec** after first cold snaps. Best booking: **Apr–Aug** shoulder. Second scam-driven demand spike follows **hurricane season (Jun–Nov)** and spring tornado outbreaks — chimney/roof damage claims pull storm-chasers in (REF, seasonal inference from AG advisory cycle).

sections.title: Price seeding (internal)
sections.markdown: Mississippi runs **among the cheapest costs of living in the nation** (MERIC Q2 2026: index 87.4 vs US 100, 6th lowest — https://meric.mo.gov/data/cost-living-data-series; World Population Review: 87.3, 2nd cheapest — https://worldpopulationreview.com/state-rankings/cost-of-living-index-by-state). Seed chimney prices **~13% below national**: sweeps toward the bottom of the national band, big-ticket relines/rebuilds discounted similarly; Jackson metro modestly above rural MS. REF — replace with direct quotes before ship (per price-research protocol).

sections.title: /rights table row (internal)
sections.markdown: License: **None for chimney work — Remodeler license only when improvements exceed $10,000 (new residential builds over $50,000), § 73-59-1** · Registration: **None below threshold** · Disclosure law: **Yes — mandatory PCDS when a licensed broker/salesperson is involved (§ 89-1-501; FSBO without a licensee not covered), §§ 89-1-501–527; form E.2 names fireplace/chimneys** · 3-day cancel / unlicensed-can't-sue: **Both — § 75-66-3 home-solicitation cancel (lost on emergency request + substantial performance) AND § 73-59-9 unlicensed can't sue (documented expenses only)** · CO law: **None statewide (smoke or CO) — local IRC/IFC only** · Lookup: https://www.msboc.us

story.heading: The story
story.markdown: Mississippi is the South's threshold-gate specimen in nearly pure form: a real board (MSBOC), a real misdemeanor penalty, a real can't-sue bar — all switched **off at $10,000 and below**, which is where almost every chimney job lives, so the practical answer to "is my sweep licensed?" is "there is no license." Meanwhile the state runs a **mandatory, unalterable MREC disclosure form that asks about fireplace/chimney defects by name** — for any sale a licensed agent touches — and its consumer act is deliberately weak (no treble, no class actions, mandatory pre-suit informal dispute settlement through an AG-approved program); the legislature instead put its muscle in criminal law, uniquely writing **"chimneys, chimney liners" into the Home Repair Fraud statute** (§ 97-23-103, felony at $10,000+). CO/smoke law is a void: the 1999 Smoke Detector Act died in committee and nothing replaced it, leaving protection to the part of the state that didn't opt out of the 2014 uniform code. **CORRELATION VERDICT: CONFIRM.** For chimney-scale work the licensing switch is off ($10,000 gate, $50,000 for new construction) and disclosure law is strong and chimney-explicit — no-license ⇄ yes-disclosure is exactly the inverse pattern.

faq.q: What should I check before hiring a chimney company in Mississippi?
faq.a: State licensing: None for chimney work — Remodeler license only when improvements exceed $10,000 (new residential builds over $50,000), § 73-59-1. Registration or credential: None below threshold. Seller disclosure at sale: Yes — mandatory PCDS when a licensed broker/salesperson is involved (§ 89-1-501; FSBO without a licensee not covered), §§ 89-1-501–527; form E.2 names fireplace/chimneys. Right to cancel a sale made at your home: see the remedies section. Carbon monoxide alarm law: None statewide (smoke or CO) — local IRC/IFC only. Where to check a contractor: https://www.msboc.us. Then ask the eight questions below, get the inspection findings in writing with photos, and never sign for "emergency" work on the day of a door-knock.

faq.q: Is a chimney inspection required when a home sells in Mississippi?
faq.a: STATE LAW: mandatory Property Condition Disclosure Statement (PCDS), Miss. Code Ann. §§ 89-1-501 through 89-1-527 (https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-89/chapter-1/real-estate-transfer-disclosure-requirements/section-89-1-509/), MREC-promulgated form that "may not be altered or personalized." Fetched the actual form (https://www.mrec.ms.gov/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/mrec_forms_PCDS_2017_FINAL-LEGAL_WITH_PAGE_NUMBERS-03-27-2017.pdf): Section E.2 asks about "past or present problems, malfunctions or defects with … fireplace/chimneys … including any modifications to them"; E.3 covers outdoor fireplaces; the Section G appliance grid lists SMOKE/MONOXIDE DETECTORS and FREE STANDING STOVE; B.7–B.8 ask whether remodels were permitted and name the licensed contractor. Scope (confirmed in statute text): § 89-1-501 applies to transfers of real property with 1–4 dwelling units (sale, exchange, installment land contract, lease with option, etc.) only "when the execution of such transfers is by, or with the aid of, a duly licensed real estate broker or salesperson" (https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-89/chapter-1/real-estate-transfer-disclosure-requirements/section-89-1-501/).

Private remedy (§ 75-24-15, https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-75/chapter-24/general-provisions/section-75-24-15/) is thin: monetary loss only — NO treble damages, NO class actions ("every private action must be maintained in the name of and for the sole use and benefit of the individual person"), and plaintiff must FIRST make "a reasonable attempt to resolve any claim through an informal dispute settlement program approved by the Attorney General."
